name: Ore Detector

pages.text: Two Heavy Cores, three Breeze Rods and a comparator. One detector replaces the eleven separate vanilla ore detectors the mod used to have.

pages.title: Scanning
pages.text: Right click a **surface** with it in your **main hand**. The beam fires straight into that face and reports what it finds in the action bar, tinted per ore. The box it swept is outlined through the rock for a couple of seconds, so you can see how far and how wide that was.

pages.title: What a scan costs
pages.text: It costs **1 durability** a scan whatever it finds, and a measure of that ore's liquid for every block found. Cheap ore is cheap to look for; valuable ore is not.

pages.title: Two pools
pages.text: **Durability** is 1000 and is mechanical wear. A Breeze Shard in an anvil restores 250, and that repair costs the same handful of levels every time. It never climbs, so a detector lasts as long as you keep finding shards.

pages.title: The tank
pages.text: **Liquid** is the tank, 500 finds across at most five ores. Hover the detector to see what is loaded and how far it reaches.

pages.title: Running dry
pages.text: Running dry does not break it. The last of a charge is spent on whatever it can still cover, that ore drops out of the tank, and the detector stops answering for it until you pour more in.

pages.title: What a bottle carries
pages.text: The tank holds **500 finds**, and one find of any ore costs one millibucket. Rarity is in the brewing, not in the reading: one dust is three bottles, so a dust of coal carries 495 finds and a dust of ancient debris carries 36.

pages.title: Brewing it
pages.text: Three bottles of a cheap ore very nearly fill the tank. An expensive one takes many more, which is the point: brew it once and you can carry as many finds of it as you like.

description: The one item the mod is named for.
